item.text: {"A":"Use the measured jj→kk→k→j locality traversal as the seed. With SIMD and OpenMP off, explore a small TILE/J_TILE tuning sweep around 32 (for example 16, 32, 64), preserving partial-tile bounds and ascending k accumulation for every output. Keep the work general across supported sizes, seeds, and repeats; validate correctness and compare full-process timings.","B":"Investigate whether SIMD can improve the contiguous-j locality path rather than assuming SIMD=1 helps: compare vectorizing across independent output columns and compiler-friendly loop forms, keeping each output's k accumulation order intact. Isolate vectorization from OpenMP and avoid duplicating A's tile-parameter search. The measured layout+SIMD candidate was slower than A's locality candidate, so retain it only if measurements show a repeatable gain without correctness regressions.","C":"Explore OpenMP over independent output rows on top of A's locality traversal. Compare contiguous static scheduling with a few reasonable static chunk choices on the 4-core ARM64 target; assess whether parallel overhead is worthwhile across supported sizes. Keep rows race-free and preserve the serial option. The measured OpenMP-only candidate was slower than A, so do not assume parallelism is beneficial.","G":"Treat A's measured 0.012896 s candidate as the current performance fallback. Integrate and measure A+C first, then A+B, and only test A+B+C if pairwise results justify it. No combination has measured interaction data yet: validate every integrated candidate and use full-process timings, retaining the fastest actually measured valid version rather than assuming gains add." ,"analysis":"The baseline measured 0.049584 s and was correct on 8 search cases. Among the reported candidates, A's reordered tiled locality path was fastest at 0.012896 s; C's OpenMP-only change measured 0.014555 s, and B's layout+SIMD change measured 0.015293 s. These results favor locality as the first optimization direction, but do not establish how SIMD or OpenMP interact with A. Keep the computation general and use measurements plus correctness validation for each change and integration."}
